escalations: E1 (S07 vs spec ~line 323): the spec says remembered approvals do not keep keys available after lock. S07 says the timed option (4/12/24 h) keeps approvals through a lock, but key access still needs an unlock. Suggest the spec distinguish approvals from key availability. Spec owner decides.
E2 (S01/S02 vs spec ~line 488): 'ssh -G evaluates configuration; Match exec may run commands' is an inference. No source sentence states it. Needs behavioral evidence from G07/G09.
E3 (S27): Bubble Tea v2 is imported as charm.land/bubbletea/v2, not github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea. Check plan or prototype text for stale paths.

E4 (S22): Iroh JS (@number0/iroh 1.1.0) publishes no macOS Intel (darwin-x64) binary, while the Rust crate lists macOS x86_64. OpenTUI core needs node >=26.4.0 or bun >=1.3.0 and has Zig native components. Relevant to the G02 distribution gate.
E5 (S32): The OpenAI Evals platform is going read-only on 2026-10-31 and shutting down on 2026-11-30. The guidance still supports the spec claim, but the platform must not be a dependency.
E6: Win32-OpenSSH has no root LICENSE file and every release is labeled Preview/Beta (latest 10.0.0.0p2-Preview, 2025-10-27). The baseline and licensing decision is for the owner.

E7: crossterm's last crates.io release (0.29.0, 2025-04-05) is 18 months old, though master is active. Its GitHub latest tag (0.28) lags crates.io. Pigeons license metadata differs: Cargo.toml says MIT OR Apache-2.0, the GitHub API says Apache-2.0. Both are recorded, not decided.
Timing note: the spec says sources were accessed on 2026-10-01. The ssh-keygen man page (S10) has an 'October 1, 2026' footer, so its content may have changed within hours of that access date.
limitations: 'supported' means the fetched page text matches the spec's one-line claim. It is not behavioral evidence about installed versions.
OpenBSD man pages expose no $Mdocdate$ and no Last-Modified header. The pin is the 'OpenBSD-current <date>' footer plus the text sha256.
1Password dateModified values track site rebuilds (S06, S09 and S12 share one timestamp), so I rely on the text hash for those.
Raw HTML hashes are advisory, because page chrome varies. The text hash was stable across two fetches about 10 minutes apart, but long-term stability is unproven.
OpenAI pages (S24, S25, S26, S31, S32, S33) are hashed from the .md variants of the same URLs.
Python, Swift and Kotlin Iroh bindings were not individually version-checked.
Docker, platform installs and builds were not needed for this task. I downloaded no artifacts and ran no candidate code.
No independent review has been done. Self-check only; the work is not independently reviewed.

summary: I pinned all 34 sources (S01-S34) and the G02 candidate dependencies. Every source fetched with HTTP 200 and its text matches the spec's one-line claim: supported 34, changed 0, not_found 0, could_not_fetch 0. I wrote `docs/sources/pins.json`, `docs/decisions/0003-source-pins.md` and `docs/sources/excerpts/notes.md`. The 34 text hashes were stable across two fetches about 10 minutes apart. Each pin is the best one available: OpenBSD footer date, HTTP Last-Modified, a docs-page date, a git commit and blob SHA, or a text sha256. Candidates are pinned with version, license and maintenance dates. They are Bubble Tea v2.0.10 (`charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, MIT), Ratatui 0.30.2, crossterm 0.29.0, OpenTUI 0.5.14, Iroh 1.3.0 plus JS 1.1.0, Pigeons v0.2.1, Win32-OpenSSH 10.0.0.0p2-Preview, step-ca v0.30.2 and step CLI v0.31.0. The ADR lists seven escalations (E1-E7). The two most consequential: S07 shows timed approvals persist through a 1Password lock (against spec ~line 323), and Iroh JS has no Intel macOS binary. No independent review has been done.
